Resolve column arguments against the data

Source: R/utils-columns.R
resolve_col.Rd

Internal helpers that turn a user-supplied column argument (an unquoted name captured with rlang::ensym() or rlang::enquo()) into the column name actually present in data. Every _col argument in sysPrep accepts both raw ESSENCE names (HospitalName) and their janitor::clean_names() equivalents (hospital_name), so users never have to know which form their data is in.

Usage

resolve_col(data, col_sym, call = rlang::caller_env())

resolve_col_optional(data, col_sym)

resolve_col_str(data, col_sym, call = rlang::caller_env())

resolve_facility_col(
  data,
  facility_col_sym,
  facility_col_missing,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

resolve_facility_col_str(
  data,
  facility_col_sym,
  facility_col_missing,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

capture_col_sym(col_quo, arg = "facility_col", call = rlang::caller_env())

as_string_or_null(col_sym)

clean_names_safe(data)

input_name_map(original_names, cleaned_names)

restore_input_names(result, name_map)

finish_names(result, clean_names, name_map)

Arguments

data

A data frame, normally already passed through clean_names_safe().

col_sym

A symbol naming a column, in raw ESSENCE or snake_case form. For as_string_or_null(), a symbol returned by resolve_col_optional(), or NULL.

call

The environment of the exported function that errors should be attributed to. Defaults to the caller's frame, so an error raised from an exported function's own call reads "Error in dedupe()" rather than "Error in resolve_col()". Wrappers forward their own call.

facility_col_sym

A symbol naming the user-supplied facility_col, or NULL when it was not supplied.

facility_col_missing

Logical. TRUE when the caller did not supply facility_col, so the Hospital-preferring default applies.

col_quo

The expression captured by rlang::enquo() for an optional column argument.

arg

The argument's name, used in the error message.

original_names, cleaned_names

The column names of the input before and after clean_names_safe(), in the same order.

result

The data frame about to be returned.

name_map

The named character vector from input_name_map(): values are original names, names are their normalized forms.

clean_names

Logical. The caller's clean_names argument.

Value

resolve_col(), resolve_col_optional(), and resolve_facility_col() return a symbol (resolve_col_optional() returns NULL when the column is absent). resolve_col_str() and resolve_facility_col_str() return a string. as_string_or_null() returns a string, or NULL for a NULL input. capture_col_sym() returns a symbol, or NULL. clean_names_safe() returns data with snake_case names and any leading-dot names kept. input_name_map() returns the named character vector described above. restore_input_names() and finish_names() return result with its column names restored or normalized.

Details

resolve_col() tries a direct match first, then normalizes both the supplied name and the data's names to snake_case and matches on that. janitor::make_clean_names() makes the names in a vector unique (two columns that would both be visit_id become visit_id and visit_id_2), so at most one column can match a given normalized name; because every exported function normalizes data first, this is always the case. It aborts, attributed to call, when nothing matches. resolve_col_optional() returns NULL instead of aborting, for functions that degrade gracefully when an optional column (for example HospitalZip) was not pulled. resolve_col_str() is resolve_col() returning a string, for .data[[...]] subsetting.

resolve_facility_col() is shared by every exported function taking a facility_col argument. When the caller did not supply facility_col (it checks this with rlang::quo_is_null() before evaluating the argument and passes the result as facility_col_missing), it prefers the stable numeric Hospital/C_BioSense_Facility_ID identifier over the mutable HospitalName display string: a facility rename or rebrand changes HospitalName but not Hospital, so grouping or joining by HospitalName can silently split one facility's rows across a rename, or merge two different facilities that briefly share a display name. An explicitly supplied facility_col is always honored exactly as given.

capture_col_sym() turns an optional, NULL-defaulting column argument, captured by the exported function with rlang::enquo(), into a symbol (or NULL when it was not supplied). Every function with a facility_col argument uses it, so the capture is written once; it aborts with a plain message, attributed to the caller, when given something other than a name (for example c(a, b)), where rlang::as_name() alone fails with an error about a captured expression.

clean_names_safe() is janitor::clean_names() that preserves leading-dot prefixes. janitor::clean_names() strips leading dots (for example .index_encounter becomes index_encounter), which would break references to the metadata columns that sysPrep itself adds (.index_encounter, .out_of_state, ...). A consequence is that a raw input column must never be given a leading-dot name: it would not normalize like other raw columns.

input_name_map(), restore_input_names() and finish_names() implement clean_names = FALSE. Every function normalizes its input names so column arguments resolve either way, which would otherwise make clean_names = FALSE a no-op on output. input_name_map() records which original name each normalized name came from (positionally, since normalization neither drops nor reorders columns); restore_input_names() renames the result's columns back through that map, leaving the columns the function itself added (.index_encounter, region_hybrid, ...) as they are; and finish_names() is the single exit that applies whichever of clean_names_safe() or the restore the caller asked for.
